Scott DesJarlais, the guy I am running against in TN-04, took two oaths.
The first was the Hippocratic oath, the doctor's promise to do no harm. The second was the congressional oath, the legislator's promise to serve the people of this district with honesty and conviction.
**He broke both.** Public records show he pressured a mistress (who was also his patient) to get an abortion. A direct, documented violation of the ethical boundary between physician and patient. Meanwhile, he spent 14 years voting to strip healthcare access from the very people who trusted him with their votes, calling the repeal of the Affordable Care Act his "number one priority."
_**After years of trying to tear down our healthcare system, has Scott DesJarlais offered a serious plan to make it better? No.**_
_**He collects a government paycheck, listens to whatever the "party lines" are and calls it leadership. Aug 1 | | | | | | | | | Scott DesJarlais, the guy I am running against in TN-04, took two oaths. The first was the Hippocratic oath, the doctor's promise to do no harm. The second was the congressional oath, the legislator's promise to serve the people of this district with honesty and conviction. He broke both. Public records show he pressured a mistress (who was also his patient) to get an abortion. A direct, documented violation of the ethical boundary between physician and patient. Meanwhile, he spent 14 years voting to strip healthcare access from the very people who trusted him with their votes, calling the repeal of the Affordable Care Act his "number one priority." After years of trying to tear down our healthcare system, has Scott DesJarlais offered a serious plan to make it better? No. He collects a government paycheck, listens to whatever the "party lines" are and calls it leadership. Tennessee deserves better. ! | | ---|---|--- Tennessee is only as strong as its most vulnerable neighbor and only as successful as the children we leave behind. That's why it's time to send career politicians like Scott DesJarlais into retirement, and usher the next generation of Congressmen that is not scared to fight for YOU. Desjarlais wore a pro-life rating like a badge of honor while operating by a completely different set of rules behind closed doors. He accepted the endorsements and cashed the checks... all while building a record that is the single greatest argument against ever giving him another term. This isn't personal. It's a pattern. A man who has spent his entire career saying one thing and doing another deserves exactly one thing in return: A pink slip from the people he was elected to serve.Let 's send someone to Washington who actually means what they say. Peter,

The Missouri primary is this Tuesday, August 4th. In just three days,

up one more time to help her win on Tuesday and reclaim her seat in

# Over 300,000 Electric Cut-Offs Pending Under Wes Moore.

# Wes Moore is focused on his own political power...but Maryland families need a governor who will keep their electric power on.
Dear friend, Never has the urgency of our need for your support been as clear as it is now. Wes Moore is a Democratic-Socialist-praising Democratic frontrunner to be president - but we can stop him here in Maryland with your help.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/17rzhOspdBL?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)

Today, _Wes Moore is building his national political profile which[AP News](https://us.list-manage.com/nXEdfB87iQX?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) is reporting clearly makes him a presidential contender by becoming the Chair of the National Governor's Association (NGA),_ which he then divisively is using to publicly lie claiming current federal interference the 2026 elections before they are even held.

And he is using his new position to push for a national "service program" for youth \- which he says will "save us as a society."1

But he can't even save someone here in Maryland from losing their electricity during the hot summer months.

It's simple. Wes Moore has a governance failure problem.

And this Monday, Wes Moore is calling legislators back to Annapolis to change Maryland’s redistricting rules and steal the voices of millions of Maryland voters. To advance his national ambitions, Wes Moore wants to make Maryland an 8-0 Democrat Representation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Meanwhile, nearly 300,000 Maryland families are facing imminent electric shutoff while also facing another proposed BGE rate increase. Where is Wes? Traveling the country campaigning while offering an offensive $12.50 in assistance to ratepayers. This electric cut-off number is up from 115,000 electric cut offs last year, 100,000 cut-offs in 2024 and similar numbers in 2023.

Wes Moore's Maryland is potentially on track to have over 500,000 electric cut-offs before the end of his term. [Help me make it his only term.](https://us.list-manage.com/14ywuyzs9w6?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b)

I will act to bring new power plants back online immediately and lower electric bills. My plan will bring closed power plants back online, expand LNG and bring online Small Modular Reactors that can efficiently power whole cities safely. SMRs are now even being considered in Pennsylvania and elsewhere, and real opportunities in this field are developing.

When we stop Wes Moore here we save both Maryland and the United States.

This is why I am asking for and need your help. [Please donate now](https://us.list-manage.com/Mwb1Kb2nTZK?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) \- any amount will help. You can also sign up to volunteer and [help us ballot chase](https://us.list-manage.com/KmhbSOAztR8?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) and win the swing votes needed to win the election.

For Maryland First,

Dan Cox
Republican Nominee for Governor of Maryland

P.S. Don't miss our [upcoming events](https://us.list-manage.com/Sfw5hOL6bry?e=5bb5efcda7&c2id=56a77d5a7be3731f6f21d9e4cc6a323b) as well. I'd love to see you there.

1\. Sound familiar? A school-to-work pipeline was first discussed as concerning in The Phyllis Schlafly Report, www. eagleforum.org, where Mrs. Schlafly detailed how it could create an "unholy alliance between big government and big corporations,” allowing bureaucrats to dictate national job placement.

([Pittsburgh Magazine, courtesy of USW](https://substack.com/redirect/a70aa2f3-c6de-47c9-8111-182579504f11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
I wrote last week about [friction](https://substack.com/redirect/a8f93ed3-b079-4c37-92ef-bfef31517844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is what you experience as a Democrat in the places I used to represent. It's impossible not to notice how dissatisfied small-town and rural western Pennsylvanians are with the national Democratic "brand."
But people like this live all over Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan -- the traditional "blue wall" -- and also Ohio and Iowa, two places you might have gotten used to conceding, but which are essential for Senate control and which will become even more important after the 2030 [redistricting](https://substack.com/redirect/2c4eadb8-01d7-4f93-ab52-a6195af1db09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I think whoever we nominate in 2028 should have a credible claim to win these people back, but framing our choice that way means talking about our shortcomings, and I suspect Democrats will be reluctant to do that. So I'll do it here.
Consider the voters of Beaver County, Pennsylvania, in my old congressional district. At one time the county's Aliquippa Works was the largest integrated steel mill in the world. ([This](https://substack.com/redirect/103568e4-4b9d-4ce6-8aa4-91bd0efdad75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a fascinating book about the local social and political history, with a focus on high school football.) The workers and their families all voted for Democrats. ...

It's impossible not to notice how dissatisfied small-town and rural western Pennsylvanians are with the national Democratic "brand." But people like this live all over Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan -- the traditional "blue wall" -- and also Ohio and Iowa, two places you might have gotten used to conceding, but which are essential for Senate control and which will become even more important after the 2030 . I think whoever we nominate in 2028 should have a credible claim to win these people back, but framing our choice that way means talking about our shortcomings, and I suspect Democrats will be reluctant to do that. So I'll do it here. Consider the voters of Beaver County, Pennsylvania, in my old congressional district. At one time the county's Aliquippa Works was the largest integrated steel mill in the world. ( is a fascinating book about the local social and political history, with a focus on high school football.) The workers and their families all voted for Democrats. ... ## Trump Puts $1.8B Fund Back on Table
President Trump said on Saturday he would renew his push to get a controversial $1.776 billion "anti-weaponization" fund codified into law [if the Senate does not confirm](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGunSAURb8GZ9zAUREHDm7TMHuddNChAT0-T4tggCt5_frG-wsd72RnrfXrY_6w5Cl8_rAHTmWLc8CaPZaCaS7pdZwJL7owS-0o5e0V1hqPGQQoLjQXMK-W_NfcNeu0IQK2DU5y0L1SPQy62aex7UTnlHRKL2sHo1TSbs6h0lIvEmRD0_0mtAApxNCrhxv7XonWjp0eQNmBdQJXKjE9fkcKZcfNf8UL02OJR-OnvZQzs_bJwDAwtdbHkcO9MTAY-CszMLcUAxPLjomBeYvx81Uy3ylzGwrxivaMgf7aQjHwW5Q7u_zhMfCyIy_WeWRgbOLPJ4wLupO1Ji60svb7tzsg1vwT09mkaT0reU9Z3eifhyX_Ri3_1fea4F8AAAD__3iUj48) his attorney general pick, Todd Blanche. The President [called out Republican Sens.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ8GOkfGYOMULrahy7ZbIgPjeFb-QfYElPv0V0S6T3DrGX3nfOffY35YDJief20EQy7PCc4agAjKTOUV9wIHHlA7vWCp7pW2M8dZcKEY14yLebMY3vPQbsYBCOhbMN2opVJSjLr1xg3CLY6DXLUcFe-hW7pOqsH13aKHTbVoLhrXXHScj1LdlruUivf2PuhRKDs2A4cNKZfb_4yJPLjwzgeU25pjG4wn2mvT_2nE1IiJPHgM4bo1YvI5wiXUiMluERNWKpYwp0ZMivNecsU-lox8AUuQKrOJkJ1g95zw6_PMlmDT6oGtOTks8YfQFrPtJ4aAVV0tn9HiJ7mlX015GPEdAAD__94Fiaw) John Cornyn (Texas) and Thom Tillis (N.C.), who have been the faces of the stalled vote. Neither Republican has committed to advancing the nomination of the acting attorney general. The [senators have refused to vote](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGupCAQRb9GdxhAAXvBYjbuerazNCWULRMEg9Ua39e_2O8T3q6Surm55_x7jk8IMaTXX1jR0pzHhOcekQjLSOW9bgWPcOAu-imUfX4nf-Z1lFxqxnvG5eghxGvsam9nRIltjVaYXmmtpOnrxbqHMJMxQoN2s3IChOSt6cTccaV8C3WwdxvvuRScG6Wb6aGU5i08ut5IDabqOPpAuTT_c0i04ByvfGBpXF7raBeiba_aP5UcKjmc59m4ab8p7n8lh_us5OBzgujZh4lR9p5NEZJbkAFRLgkv9sKEBSJzOc2hrEAhJ0YhxrAzl0u6EoNEgZ0IW07h6ydwO6nkUBfrt_MT1vfk1wohfibSr7weVn4HAAD__76Hj9k) for Blanche unless it is put in writing that Trump will no longer pursue the fund, which was negotiated with the IRS as a settlement for Trump's tax returns being leaked. Trump suggested on Thursday that he could[ temporarily withdraw Blanche's nomination](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnwZ3RsoDtFC6uocu1VyKDl-CTwZG9wcrb_0pe4a9H-kYz_-7z3YUYzsdfd5DlLc0n1RKJmfLM-XU8M13hotKZJeSyvU5f0zEjoJJgJODsXYjveRDebkRIvSDbaTMqNaI2YrcrAHYDYI_L4PVi9NYRuHUbVq-1d14E-9HAAHYAelTtchtHBb27DUajcroZgHzglNv_KZy80xbf6aLcrukQ0e7Mz9L0fxqcGpxqra1L8ZM1OLnMYY1UGpy-Y2Rx7yLX9Ipe1sC7z65K3umU3dgDGgBodz6iyNY_a4gxFPXpfxwufE3BvzrpsvgTAAD__1vLews) and resubmit it after Tillis and Cornyn leave the Senate next year.
## FIFA Kills Plan To Sell Stake in World Cup
In a reversal of plans from earlier in the week, FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Friday that the international soccer governing body had scrapped a plan [to sell stakes in future competitions](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOpCAYhJ8Gb3TgR1APHDa7cU891zkahJ9uJigGUOPbT5xXmGtVUvnq-3xOTxNiWF8fZkFdfZpWPEvEWjFPNe_LlvEIBxbezyEXv6_uTMsEDBRlPWUwORPiNbWN0x4RUDSoeddLpSR0ffPWsu-MbQfuxcw5H8C3nivplW3nls_WNUHfa6xnwBnrpHrMg5SKCTO0fQfKdKRl6EJN-fGVwlrf6OOVDswPm5Ym6netWyHiD4GRwGhmez-4OwLj_-cd_91j3TMSGHf0hs7psqlWeqYcHbX7Rn3whtq01rDuWOgWzUoLxkhgLDXli4gxOCL-cSFBcCl4k7XbzhBjKOrmey0mxB-e-iuJh4bvAAAA__-gBYTo) to private investors. Infantino had proposed creating a $20 billion company to run the World Cup with private investors but [drew backlash that grew every day](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuOszAQhZ8GOqLJAL4ULv4mXf52S-TLOJmVsZFxiPL2K_YVtjw60rl8X_flbjlxfvy3K5kWy5LpvSdqjerS6mvdKh180H5VjuseXzm8y7ogoBhADYBLsJw-y9QHE4mQxp7MVapZiBml6p8GbSRQFILCmbSYXRSkJ4d2jF548j2bMw0U4BVAzuLi9DwLGK2elERhZTcBBW6lXr4L5_akmD7loHrxZe2Teba27d34r8Nbhze7nQdO6xS1sU_U4Y1ztLlxLkPkaIcXRTs4kCE65zyQ1F6A1YBBxgAENGqn-2rC9uaUeBfniMdqOf2Wtj-ROgz-BAAA__8F53xa) since Tuesday's announcement. The fallout from the debacle could eventually bring an end to [Infantino's decade-long presidency.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiPTgM0EDi4hm0svRA1uD31rbGR7QPP3K_YXNiuppNKr9-85P5E9h9df3MkUF-dAV_ZUCqW5pPd-JDr5pNyOC6fs3sFecZ9BghJyFBJmi-w_c19b44iAuppMq8dBqQH0WG_mofputK3TrVJuJWmVVpZAUu_02neqZnOvyVFCK6UeVLM8hkHJDh_9qEGhrnpJlktMzf_IoWzk_CeelJo17rU3WylHrro_FUwVTNd1NeuS7xd3X8F0xwqmNzkUjh0KDiflslMo4vAYRF4THgdZ8WIMgQUHh6FwiGLB9ctj3iqY6mTscbH3nNVN9NqR_Q9B-ZW208B3AAAA__-2EoLh) Aleksander Čeferin, president of European soccer body UEFA, said _"No option should be off the table. "_ The organization said it welcomed the decision to [withdraw the plan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOhCAUheGnwW7M9SqIBcU2drPtlgbhMsMuigFGMm-_cV9h65OcL_m_7std--D3x6feSBUXl51qDlQKpaWk13YkOv1JuZOrT9m9dlvjtiCguIG8AS5W-_BehsYqR4TUN6S6UXIhOI6yeSqDgIZzN1mURoiug1F2sEqcHMnBQuPV9QYSsAMYuWjXiXMBvZ4GOaLQIxuArC8xtd_R7-VJLrzjSak1cWuCepZyZNZ_MJwZzrXWdl3NtTGc8xFTYTi7GMuqQ2A461S8CZQZzgaGn4T72Z99bJKyR_Uh-Cwu8bFpH_6E8q8sp8LfAAAA___m9XU4), calling it "a victory for the whole game."
## Women's Pro Baseball Takes the Field
The nation's first women's professional baseball league in nearly 30 years [opened its inaugural season Saturday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOiMzBBsKF2nosu2WyMRjmKx_kG1AefsV9xVuN9IZHR19f1_zS5OjsP7RHlWxcQ54ZYelYJpLOvye8KQTczsslLI9grmin4GDYHxgHGajyX3nR22URQTsalStHHohepBDvam3HDk3KDorNABabji3nexaLY1oe12Tum184NByLnvRLGPfC97p8TFIEFpWD46GSkzNJ1IoG1r3jSem5h197dRWyp6r7lnBVMF0XVfjc7hZBRMGduQKprzHVO7Du-V-ih4Dy2xPkS0646KdYw71eiAzuBwls7JRZhfiPwyGUWB5TxRWS-gMI-coRLp9OrHnE0b9-VKdlNmvm2VxN69ek_tpLL8a9lTwPwAA__9hqo5F) with the Los Angeles Queens facing the New York Heights before a sold-out crowd in Springfield, Illinois. A pro women's baseball team last toured the country in the mid-1990s, in the wake of the success of the movie _A League of Their Own_. The new 2026 four-team [Women's Pro Baseball League ](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ8GOqLxYOyhcHGbdLntlsgO4-CVwch2QHn7FfsKWx4d6fx8X4_pYUMM2-u_XdlUn6aNzxK5Vs5Tze91z3yEg4sgF3Lx720-0zohoOqAOsBptiF-JtnOxjMj9y0boWlQakBN7WJICSmEk_0AWjkg8ND35MmRdD0J2wZzpQEBCgA9qJsbh0FBb0dJGpXVjQSeQ0359p3CVhf28ZMOzrdnWttollr30vT_Grw3eLf7deCyLpFreEZu8H6mlbfSOVvY2Ri7JZSa8qc7dxc7DY69BSTFOLJXmgTIp7c8KkI1UpvNvJ8hxlDUtea12hB_2-ufkB0GfwIAAP__ZP99WQ)also includes the Boston Hunters and San Francisco Firebells. Every regular-season and playoff game will be played at 5,200-seat Robin Roberts Stadium, connecting the new league to Springfield, a city whose women's baseball history dates to 1875. All [37 games](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD0O2zAMRk9jbwxkOZaUQUOXbOna0aAtylGhH0OUE-T2hdPeoCOBxwe879djfmCIIW8_MZFtvsyZ3hypNapzq0faK73Ci3gwS6jsj-zeJc1SSAXCgJCzwxA_87V31hNJGnuygzaTUpPUpn9apYaFVj1qqZS-XY0YHXphjJluk6Z17YM9bcIIOQihJ3VZbtOkxIi3q9FSoe6uglxopV5-l5Dbk3z8lBfVy1pSH-2ztZ278Ucn7528E-95r8RcS0kn0cn794ZKkZDpHwNM61GJIZELCDVsz8bQCrxLosyw1wILMi0YI0TC7SBYashbyBv4I0ZgQi4ZMDvYI36K99__v_KGtZ0kHtvBDYZO3vtq3f4OMQZWZ9OWMMRvQ_uv4V9W_gkAAP__Mmqbww), including September's best-of-five championship series, will stream on ESPN, while 11 regular-season games will be simulcast on Scripps Sports Network.

**Whatever happened to Salisbury steak?** The gravy-smothered ground beef patty that once symbolized modern American convenience actually started as a health food. Its slide from TV-dinner star to cafeteria punchline is one of the great demotions in culinary history. Salisbury steak is named for Dr. James Henry Salisbury, a 19th-century New York physician and [early germ-theory researcher](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAQxfHTQGZkCvxB4GATst50Q2Sg3NSOwS27APXtRz1XmPzp6af_v8f08BTpeP71OzoOaTrwLhGZMU-cz_2V8aILS2tnyiWcx3qnfQIJWkgrJEyrp_ie-np1ARGwq9G1xiqtFRhbb04ZK_tWgjaDMa1ScujMsvYBls6HoOaa3OdNWgmtlEbpZh6U0rLzQ28NaG-qXuJKnHLzP9HBG4b4ThfmZkl7Hd3G_CpV96eCsYLxvu-m7MRbSQf5Y_fPz6yC0WcuYjkjnxkrGIuPVOYzv0Vh9F9ioYuiuH0WG_rImwgpraK1yvaD6SoY6-zW100xUtEf0nP3FH8I_Ktul4PvAAAA__8zyIFi) who became convinced during the Civil War that vegetables and starches were poisoning people from the inside out. His prescription: lean minced beef three times a day, washed down with hot water. He published his findings in 1888, setting off one of America's earliest fad diets. The name stuck for good during World War I, when anti-German sentiment made "hamburger steak" sound unpatriotic. By mid-century, Salisbury steak had found its true calling: the frozen TV dinner. When [Swanson rolled out its aluminum-tray meals in the 1950s](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL9GZLiGAQkIFFxC5ksvpCRrZOZWSJQk4_Lfb7G_sFkHXd2v3r_7ejccOD7_mp109WmN9C6BaqW81vzaj0wnn1S6yXIu_hXdO-0rAqoWphZwdYbDZx0apz0RUt-Q7sZJKiVxnJpNo0SDOM8PZQc_OzmCVRJ6sGhnaR01rK81mAA7gFGqm52lVNCbeZhGVGYUA5DjmvLtf-JYN_Lhk07Kt0fam6C3Wo8i-j8CF4FL4f0IFNjTRiZXihyf5WoKXBBQClxgFrh0V0rBtd6UjVMk1xYTuNhX_rSlkvlqMz34IIFLk7U73hwCF3XRPHfD4ee9_krZqfE7AAD__1r_fvs), those gravy-bathed patties became comfort food for a generation eating in front of _I Love Lucy_. But the format that made it famous eventually dragged it down. As Americans embraced global cuisine and health-conscious eating, the dish became shorthand for everything processed and institutional, the dreaded "mystery meat" on a cafeteria tray. It hasn't vanished, though. It's just gone undercover. Chains like Bob Evans and LongHorn Steakhouse [have it on the menu](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOpDAQheHTQAYyZbBN4GATst50Q1SGoqkdAy27APXtRz1XmPhJ75P-f4_xgRx5f_7Fjbwsx7jTnSOJUBolndsr0cUX5cYFTnk59_k-thEUmEq5SsE4I8f32JazX4iAdEm-sa4zpgPrytWHtm36oGDRk25Q95ZcQFwmjX3fumBL9p835RQ0StnO1KHvOqM09q2zYNAWraKZ5Uj1_4N3WWmJ7-OiVE_HVka_irxyof8UMBQw3PddE4qsnD97AUOgLFWiLHgm3KWaVuQ9Vxkj53Cmd5WF8KuAoUx-ft0cI2fzQZ8bcvxB5FdlLg_fAQAA___H93i4), often rebranded as "chopped steak." Stauffer's and other frozen-food vendors also [still stock the frozen version](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGngc7IGGygcHEbur1tSmSWmWUSg5FnFrR5-mjzCqmPdD7p_7hNt0CR9sf_sIEXTNMOF0cQgTxJfm5HhpNO4LqfKTM-9-VK22S0cUr3SptpCRRfU1suHgEMNCX4uuutc9Z0fbn64d6ia7DB1tUOYQaj9bxYi9iidXooyb_fdK9NrXVnXTUP1jrdhKHtO-NCV7QaFpKUq89Eu6yA8ZVOyNU9bWX0q8jBRfOvMGNhxuu6KggiK_F7L8w4A4vCnL5hVxwi8fzML8UC4YtVhhDVDICK13QckLkwY5n9clwUI7F7648tUPzV5E-JTm9-AgAA__8vInwQ), and home cooks have given it a nostalgia-fueled revival online. The gravy-smothered ground beef patty that once symbolized modern American convenience actually started as a health food. Its slide from TV-dinner star to cafeteria punchline is one of the great demotions in culinary history. Salisbury steak is named for Dr. James Henry Salisbury, a 19th-century New York physician and who became convinced during the Civil War that vegetables and starches were poisoning people from the inside out. His prescription: lean minced beef three times a day, washed down with hot water. He published his findings in 1888, setting off one of America's earliest fad diets. The name stuck for good during World War I, when anti-German sentiment made "hamburger steak" sound unpatriotic. By mid-century, Salisbury steak had found its true calling: the frozen TV dinner. When , those gravy-bathed patties became comfort food for a generation eating in front of I Love Lucy. But the format that made it famous eventually dragged it down. As Americans embraced global cuisine and health-conscious eating, the dish became shorthand for everything processed and institutional, the dreaded "mystery meat" on a cafeteria tray. It hasn't vanished, though. It's just gone undercover. Chains like Bob Evans and LongHorn Steakhouse , often rebranded as "chopped steak." Stauffer's and other frozen-food vendors also , and home cooks have given it a nostalgia-fueled revival online. Salisbury steak isn't gone, just demoted from the main stage to a quiet corner of the comfort food canon. Did you ever have a Salisbury steak frozen dinner, or try Salisbury steak in a restaurant? ## Texas Orders Halt to Border Clearing
Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham ordered U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) on Friday to [stop a contractor](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO5CAMhp-GdIyAJEAKimvo9torIyd2EnQERsDO7rz9KaO5J9jKxaff9v_9-Zg_IMSQ9t9wkmvfW54TfdVIrVGZa4NGB8RWl1yQyhoJSkj7MiuhNBeWCzUjhPichw7dInCSHTlp7Ki1HUfVHU5bmHowCKuWtBrZj8syEdphwmGjyXTBXcuEFUpKoXp5k2bSwm5kcdRo0LJBEIaWy60d1Ogb6haf-UHltuazi-5o7V5Z_4spz5T_-whwAab81YQp_4ow5a8zTHlhmPK9_A94hIR8zecZag05UeGVEla-ElTiF0SqoTa-5cIhRtoJebgmxHf4rYWHxI9PrHdqB1_zZ2pPpnxXHN6_QoyhasMGsZ8Q4uv19jPhD6f-BQAA__9Uopa7) from clearing state land in Presidio County for the border wall. The General Land Office says Barnard Construction trespassed across several sections of a 10,000-acre grazing lease and used heavy equipment to blade the terrain and strip every plant in its path. "_We will work with our federal partners to keep the southern border secured, but we will not compromise the integrity of Texas state property to do it,_ " Buckingham said. She wants the ground restored to its original condition. Buckingham's order comes after Presidio and the county's economic development group [sued the federal government](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3yoyAUBfCnwQ4HbhRJQbENXbbd0kG5KLMoGbgTk7ff0Z08wb8-cz_O789jfLiY4r78dhsaeoc87njUhERYxkqOcHWJ6pSLxzIndCXuyzSCAMWF5gJG72L6jF3jzST8XTZo5KB7pXTfQ7MaFZQGPwxC333AGbtJ6VliF1zfOx_mJppzmdACpBRwk60c7krogNr3yg9es06gj5RLSysSvl0N6ZNfWNo5b00yK9GzstsvBpaBPY6j_VsdnSEDe7ZhYK8xBvY8xcCKgYG9yW_Ak9s9n_O2xVpj3rHwq2_lAX3llHml_OQxJVxcSh_-heCXEP-vw6m4mRjYphj_PGJKsaqBdWLZXEzXs_Qz4peBfwEAAP__33iSOg) over the Big Bend barrier plan, arguing the barriers will cause flooding along the Rio Grande.
## Equipment Causes Methodist Hospital Fire
Houston firefighters carried extinguishers and buckets of water up the stairs of [Houston Methodist's Centennial Tower](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u5CAQBk-DM0aAbcABwSbOZtMNrba7GSNhY0Frfm6_mneFF3_SV6X6d1_ukHI6H3_hoMDvWJaTXi0TM9WlMTDtkLmtpSLVLRPUdD7WxShjpfJSmQUh5c8ydBhWhZPuKGjnR2v9OJpuD8oqBz2B89voV2f9BAjRwQDTZjGaLoXvmfLKaK1Mr2_aTVb5SB5Hiw69GBRh4lJvvBPTG1rMn_KketvK0eWwM19N9H-EmYWZYd10_12Ema_SWJh5q_RqslK7yokypkqylhLlQbwXTI3lXtqVGLLcI8oGnybMrL8WfhiFmbsa8HqlnFOzTgzqcUDKP3T-XbNnMP8DAAD__28WgK0) on Friday because the high-rise's fire pipes were dry. The call came in just after 5 p.m., to the wrong address. Crews who found their way to the Texas Medical Center tower met heavy fire and smoke on the roof and pulled a second alarm. Fire pipes were without water because the tower is under construction, so firefighters hauled what they could up to the fire by hand while working with building staff to get the pipes flowing. Once the pipes had water, the fire was put out. It never reached the floors below, and nobody was hurt. name: Roy Cooper
subject: A longer email
body:
10,000 votes 10 years ago
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk822_rs&source=&t=1&akid=2342%2E124072%2EVJ5n5u)
| | | |
---
Peter,
At the end of this message, I’m going to ask you to chip in $5 to my Senate campaign here in North Carolina. [**_If you’re ready to give now, you can use this link to donate._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk822_rs&amount=5&t=8&akid=2342%2E124072%2EVJ5n5u)
**Otherwise, please let me explain why your support is so important and what could happen without it.**
In 2016, I ran for Governor for the first time.
I was fighting to unseat Republican Governor Pat McCrory. Nobody had defeated an incumbent Governor in North Carolina for more than 150 years, but I knew that we had the team behind us to win and make history.
Throughout the race, multiple election experts were saying it was a “Toss Up.” Poll after poll showed me with a slight – or sometimes even large – lead. The momentum was on our side.
**However, on election night, the race was too close to call.**
I ended that night with a less than 5,000-vote lead – which might sound like a lot but is a razor-thin margin in North Carolina, especially given the 4.6 million ballots cast. It was less than half of 1%.
Governor McCrory didn’t concede. He claimed that there had been voter fraud in our state with no evidence to back it up.
He called for a recount, and over the next month, he and his team continued spreading baseless conspiracy theories and undermining faith in the democratic process.
**Yet on Dec. 5, 2016, democracy won. The recount was wrapped up, and the results were in: We had won the race by 10,277 votes.**
Peter, this current Senate race is starting to remind me a lot of my 2016 race.
Just like in 2016, the momentum today appears to be on our side.
The polls show me with a slight advantage, and experts have increased our odds of winning. Even though President Trump carried North Carolina each of the three times he ran, the experts are saying that this is the best chance for Democrats to flip a Republican-held seat in the country.
Here’s what worries me...
**We could have just as easily lost that race in 2016. Despite all of the winds blowing in our favor, we still only won by 10,277 votes – just 0.22%.**
That’s why we simply cannot take our foot off the gas. We cannot look at the polls and the predictions and think for a second that we have this in the bag. We cannot give our Republican opponent or the right-wing super PACs supporting him an inch.
**I won in 2016 – in the same election that President Trump first won the presidency – only because of grassroots support from people like you. That’s how I plan to win again, but I need you with me.**
[**_Please, Peter: Will you chip in $5, or whatever you can, today to help us flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk822_rs&amount=5&t=9&akid=2342%2E124072%2EVJ5n5u)

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.
